questions.subject: BUSINESS_ENTREPRENEURSHIP
questions.learningObjective: Compare legal forms of business
questions.stem: Alderwood, a small bike accessories maker in Chicago, wants owners to have limited liability but avoid double taxation. Which business form best fits?

options.text: A general partnership, where each partner risks only their investment
options.misconception: Mistakes a general partnership for a limited-liability structure

options.text: A corporation, whose profits are taxed only once at the owner level
options.misconception: Believes corporate income escapes entity-level taxation

options.text: A sole proprietorship, which shields owners from all business debts
options.misconception: Assumes a sole proprietorship provides limited liability

options.text: An LLC, which limits owner liability and is taxed like a partnership

questions.explanation: An LLC combines limited liability for owners with pass-through taxation, so profits are taxed once on owners' returns. A sole proprietorship and a general partnership expose owners to unlimited personal liability, while a corporation faces entity-level tax and then dividend tax.
questions.hint: Look for the form that pairs limited liability with pass-through taxation.
